blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
. Decompositional scene reconstruction aims to reconstruct high-quality objects and background, yet existing methods still struggle with the level of quality under heavy occlusions. While generative priors offer a potential solution, 2D image-based priors often suffer from multi-view inconsistency due to a lack of 3D awareness. Conversely, 3D-native priors provide stronger structural inductive biases but frequently lead to spatial drift and misalignment within complex scenes.
To address these issues, we propose DecomVoxel , formulating object completion as a guided in-situ denoising optimization that bridges 3D-native priors with neural scene reconstruction. Our framework introduces a reformulated epsilon-based distillation loss to ensure stable latent refinement, alongside adaptive spatial guidance that utilizes occupied and vacant anchors with temporal annealing to suppress generative hallucinations and mitigate spatial drift. Experiments on Replica and ScanNet++ show that DecomVoxel significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods while faithfully preserving the original spatial layout, structural fidelity, and style-consistent texture. Our method pushes the boundary of decompositional reconstruction by delivering high-quality textured meshes with clean topology, geometry, and appearance, providing a robust solution for the decompositional reconstruction of complex real-world scenes.
Code is available at https://github.com/DecomVoxel/DecomVoxel .
blocks.zh:
。 。 。 。 分解场景重建旨在重建高品质的物体和背景,然而,现有方法仍然与重掩蔽下的质量水平相抗衡. 虽然基因前科提供了一个潜在的解决方案,但基于2D图像的前科由于缺乏3D意识,往往出现多视图不一致. 相反地,3D-内在前传提供了更强烈的结构诱导偏差,但往往导致复杂场景中的空间漂移和错位.
为了解决这些问题,我们提议DecomVoxel, 将对象的完成作为引导性现场解析优化, 将3D本地前身与神经场景重建相接。 我们的框架引入了重新调整的以epsilon为基础的蒸馏损失,以确保稳定的潜在改进,同时提供适应性的空间指导,利用占用和空置的锚与时滞来抑制基因幻觉并减缓空间漂移。 关于复制和ScanNet++的实验显示,DecomVoxel在忠实地维护原始空间布局,结构忠实,风格一致的纹理的同时,显著地超越了最先进的方法. 我们的方法推动分解重建的分界线,通过提供高质量的有纹理的有清洁地貌,几何,外观等特征的元片来进行分解重建,为复杂现实世界场景分解重建提供了有力的解决方案.

blocks.en: 1. Introduction
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 导言

blocks.en:
While rapid progress in neural 3D representations ( Mildenhall et al., 2020 ; Kerbl et al., 2023 ) has revolutionized holistic scene reconstruction, recent approaches ( Wu et al., 2022 ; Wu et al., 2023 ; Kong et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2023c ) have shifted focus towards decompositional reconstruction to recover individual object entities, facilitating fine-grained interaction for downstream embodied AI tasks ( Li et al., 2024 ; Lu et al., 2025a ) .
However, these methods struggle with incomplete geometry and incoherent appearances, due to inevitable occlusions and limited sensor viewpoints in real-world environments.
blocks.zh:
虽然神经3D表达法(Mildenhall等,2020年;Kerbl等,2023年)的快速进步使整体场景重建发生了革命性的变化,但最近的做法(Wu等,2022年;Wu等,2023年;Kong等,2023年;Li等,2023年c)将重点转向分解重建以恢复单个物体实体,为下游包含的AI任务提供精细的相互作用(Li等,2024年;Lu等,2025a年).
然而,这些方法与不完全的几何和不连贯的外观相冲突,这是由于在现实世界环境中不可避免的被隔离和感官视角有限.

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, recent methods ( Ni et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025b ) leverage generative priors from pre-trained image diffusion models ( Rombach et al., 2022 ; Liu et al., 2023 ) to complete missing visual and geometric content. However, due to their view-independent formulation and lack of 3D awareness, these image-based 2D priors often fail to produce coherent 3D objects or consistent appearances. In contrast, another line of work ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Xia et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) employs 3D generative models ( Zhang et al., 2023a ; Lai et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025c ) that encode geometric and structural priors from large-scale 3D datasets ( Deitke et al., 2023 ) for object completion.
Nevertheless, despite better capturing coherent 3D geometry, these 3D-native priors struggle to maintain precise spatial alignment and texture fidelity within complex scene contexts, due to the lack of explicit guidance and global constraints to regularize the inherent stochasticity of generative priors.
blocks.zh:
为了应对这些挑战,最近的方法(Ni等人,2025年;Yang等人,2025年b)利用经过预先训练的图像传播模型(Rombach等人,2022年;Liu等人,2023年)的遗传学前科,完成缺失的视觉和几何内容。 然而,由于这些基于图像的2D前传往往无法产生相通的3D对象或相通相通的外观,因此它们的视图独立配方和缺乏3D意识. 相形之下,另一行工作(Yu等,2025;Xia等,2026;Chen等,2025)采用3D基因模型(Zhang等,2023a;Lai等,2025;Li等,2025c)来编码大型3D数据集的几何和结构前身(Deitke等,2023)来完成对象.
尽管如此,尽管更好地捕捉了连贯的3D几何,这些3D-内在的前身在复杂的场景背景中为保持精确的空间对接和纹理忠实而挣扎,原因是缺乏明确的指导和全球制约,无法使基因前身的内在花纹规范化.

blocks.en:
In this paper, we propose DecomVoxel , a framework that bridges this gap by formulating the completion of missing regions in decompositional reconstruction as a guided in-situ denoising optimization to harness 3D-native priors with neural scene reconstruction.
We design the optimization pipeline that leverages structured scene representations, i.e . , sparse voxel ( Sun et al., 2025 ) , which provides flexibility to seamlessly connect with state-of-the-art 3D object generation models ( Xiang et al., 2025b ) . To effectively leverage the generative power, we propose a reformulated epsilon-based distillation loss for flow matching, where we demonstrate that optimizing the noise residual implicitly introduces a principled temporal weighting to the optimizing gradient of the latent feature. This formulation improves convergence stability and detailed geometry recovery compared with standard velocity-based optimization.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们提出DecomVoxel, 这个框架通过在分解重建中制定完成缺失区域的工作来弥补这一差距, 作为指导性的就地解析优化, 利用3D本地前科进行神经场景重建。
我们设计了利用结构化场景表现的优化管线,即:稀有活塞(Sun等,2025年),为与最先进的3D出品模型无缝连接提供了灵活性(Xiang等,2025b.). 为了有效地利用基因力量,我们提议重新制定以埃普西隆为基的蒸馏法来进行流量匹配,我们在此表明,优化噪音残留意味着对潜在特征的优化梯度进行原则性的时间加权。 与标准速度优化相比,这种配制提高了趋同稳定性和详细的几何恢复.

blocks.en: To regularize the inherent stochasticity of generative priors, which can lead to spatial drift and geometric misalignment, we introduce adaptive spatial guidance to steer the optimization through non-uniform spatial constraints and temporal annealing. Specifically, we define occupied anchors within regions of high-confidence reconstruction to preserve coherence with observations, and vacant anchors where a re-distributed pruning strategy prevents the generative model from hallucinating in zones where the object must not exist. We employ an annealing schedule that dynamically decays noise levels and guidance weights to balance generative capacity and spatial constraints, facilitating structural completion in early stages and fine-grained refinement as the latent state converges toward the clean manifold.
blocks.zh: 将基因前科的内在地貌特征规范化,这会导致空间漂移和几何错位,我们引入了适应性的空间取向,通过非统一空间约束和时间厌离来引导优化. 具体地说,我们界定了在高信心重建区域内的被占用锚地,以保持与观测的一致性,并界定了空置锚地,在这些锚地上,再分配的回旋策略可以防止基因模型在一定不存在物体的地区产生幻觉。 我们采用了一个反射时间表,动态地衰减噪声水平和指导权重,以平衡基因能力和空间限制,促进结构在早期阶段的完成和精细的改进,随着潜在状态向清洁多面性汇合。

blocks.en: We evaluate our method on the Replica ( Straub et al., 2019 ) and ScanNet++ ( Yeshwanth et al., 2023 ) datasets. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that DecomVoxel consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both geometry and appearance quality, particularly in challenging, heavily occluded scenarios. Unlike existing baselines that suffer from geometric distortion and scene-level spatial misalignment, our approach faithfully preserves the original spatial layout, structural fidelity, and style-consistent texture. Notably, our method produces high-fidelity textured meshes with clean topology, complete geometry, and consistent appearance , providing a robust solution for the decompositional reconstruction of complex real-world scenes, as shown in Figure 1 .
blocks.zh: 我们对复制品(Straub等人,2019年)和ScanNet++的方法进行评估 (Yeshwanth等,2023)数据集. 全面的实验表明,DecomVoxel在几何学和外观质量方面,特别是在具有挑战性且严重隐蔽的情景中,其业绩始终高于最先进的基线。 与受几何扭曲和场地级空间错位影响的现有基线不同,我们的方法忠实地保持了原有的空间布局,结构的忠实,风格一致的纹理. 如图1所示,我们的方法可以产生高精度的纹理,具有干净的地貌、完整的几何和连贯的外观。

blocks.en: In summary, our main contributions are as follows: • We propose DecomVoxel , formulating decompositional reconstruction as an guided in-situ denoising optimization that integrates 3D-native priors with neural scene reconstruction. • We introduce an epsilon-based distillation objective coupled with adaptive spatial guidance, which applies spatial regularization through temporal annealing to effectively suppress generative hallucinations and mitigate spatial drift. • Extensive experiments on Replica and ScanNet++ demonstrate that DecomVoxel achieves state-of-the-art performance. Our framework consistently produces high-fidelity results with clean topology, geometry, and appearance, striking a principled balance between neural scene reconstruction and 3D-native priors.
blocks.zh: 简而言之,我们的主要贡献如下: 我们提议DecomVoxel, 将分解重建作为指导性的就地解析优化, 将3D-本地前身与神经场景重建结合起来。 我们引入了以epsilon为基础的蒸馏目标,并辅之以适应性的空间取向,该目标通过时间反射来应用空间调节,以有效抑制基因幻觉并减缓空间漂移. • 关于复制品和ScanNet++的广泛实验表明,DecomVoxel达到了最先进的性能。 我们的框架以干净的地貌、几何和外观不断产生高真实度的结果,在神经场景重建与3D-本土前身之间达成原则性平衡。

blocks.en: 2. Related Work
blocks.zh: 2. 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1. 3D Scene Representation and Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 2.1. 国家 3D 场景代表和重建

blocks.en:
The rapid advancement of neural implicit representations, such as nerf ( nerf ) ( Mildenhall et al., 2020 ) and 3dgs ( 3dgs ) ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) , has significantly enhanced the fidelity of scene reconstruction from 2D images ( Müller et al., 2022 ; Yu et al., 2022 ; Yang et al., 2025c ; Li et al., 2023b ; Lu et al., 2024b ; Huang et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024a ) . To further provide more structured and manageable 3D representations, recent works have explored sparse voxel-based differentiable rendering ( Sun et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Oh et al., 2025 ; Chi et al., 2026 ) .
To facilitate downstream interactions such as object editing ( Chen et al., 2024b ; Li et al., 2025b ) , manipulation ( Lu et al., 2024a ; Li et al., 2024 ) , and simulation ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2023a ) , substantial efforts ( Wu et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2023c ; Lyu et al., 2024 ; Ye et al., 2024 ; Gu et al., 2024 ; Shen et al., 2025 ) have shifted towards decompositional scene reconstruction, which aims to extract individual 3D representations for each object and the background.
However, existing methods typically struggle to recover complete geometries, particularly in occluded regions. To address this limitation, we integrate a 3D-native prior into a voxel-based neural reconstruction framework, enabling the model to recover missing structures in situ while faithfully preserving scale and spatial alignment.

为了便利下游的相互作用,如物体编辑(Chen等,2024b;Li等,2025b),操纵(Lu等,2024a;Li等,2024),和模拟(Xie等,2024;Li等,2023a),大量努力(Wu等,2023;Li等,2023c;Lyu等,2024;Ye等,2024;Gu等,2024;Shen等,2025),转向分解场景重建,旨在提取每个物体和背景的个人3D表示.

blocks.en: 2.2. Generative Priors for Decompositional Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 2.2. 分解重建的遗传历程

blocks.en:
To achieve complete object reconstruction in occluded areas, several methods ( Chung et al., 2023 ; Huang et al., 2025b ; Yao et al., 2025 ; Dong et al., 2025 ) have explored incorporating generative priors into decompositional reconstruction. Some works ( Chen et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2023 ; Qiu et al., 2024 ; Weber et al., 2024 ) utilize 2D diffusion models to fill missing 3D information; however, they often struggle with multi-view inconsistency ( Ni et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025b ; Xia et al., 2025 ) , leading to the Janus problem ( Shi et al., 2023 ; Lin et al., 2023 ) . With the recent flourish of 3D-native generative models ( Hong et al., 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2023a ; Ye et al., 2025 ; Xiang et al., 2025a ) , another branch of research ( Meng et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026 ; Dong et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ; Zadaianchuk et al., 2026 ) seeks to ensure inherent 3D consistency by directly leveraging these 3D-native priors. For instance, MetaScenes ( Yu et al., 2025 ) and SimRecon ( Xia et al., 2026 ) utilize image-to-3D models ( Tochilkin et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ; Lai et al., 2025 ) to generate meshes, while Amodal3R ( Wu et al., 2025b ) incorporates masks as auxiliary conditions to enhance generation quality under heavy occlusion.
However, their resulting geometry and textures frequently deviate from the original observations by using 3D generative models as separate modules. Furthermore, these methods require a post-hoc alignment process to transform the meshes back into the scene coordinates. Together, these limitations lead to cumulative errors that degrade overall reconstruction quality. To address them, our method reformulates the completion of missing regions as an in-situ denoising optimization rather than a pipeline of decoupled generation and alignment. By optimizing directly within the scene coordinates, we eliminate the need for error-prone alignment and ensure seamless spatial consistency between the generated and observed regions.
blocks.zh:
为了在占地地区完成物体重建,一些方法(Chung等人,2023年;Huang等人,2025年b;Yao等人,2025年;Dong等人,2025年)已探索将基因前科纳入分解重建。 一些著作(Chen等,2023;Liu等. 2023; 邱等. ;Weber等,2024)使用2D扩散模型来填充缺失的3D信息;然而,它们经常会与多视角不一致而挣扎(Ni等,2025;Yang等,2025b;Xia等,2025),导致Janus问题(Shi等,2023;Lin等,2023.). 随着最近3D-本土基因模型的兴起(Hong等,2023;Zhang等,2023a; Ye等,2025;Xiang等,2025a.),又一研究分支(Meng等,2025;Chen等,2026;Dong等,2026;Lin等,2026;Zadaianchuk等,2026)通过直接利用这些3D-亲历者,力求确保固有的3D一致性. 例如,MetaScenes(Yu等,2025年)和SimRecon(Xia等,2026年)利用图像到3D模型(Tochilkin等,2024年;Zhang等,2024年;Lai等,2025年)生成中母体,而Amoto3R(Wu等,2025年b)则将口罩作为辅助条件,以提高重隐蔽下生成质量。
然而,它们所产生的几何和纹理经常会以3D基因模型作为单独的模块来偏离原来的观测. 此外,这些方法需要经过后热调和过程,才能将网状网回变为场景坐标. 这些限制加在一起导致累积错误,使总体重建质量下降. 为了解决这些问题,我们的方法将完成缺失区域的工作重新定位为现场解职优化,而不是脱钩生成和调整的管道。 通过在现场坐标内直接优化,我们消除了容易出错的对接需要,确保生成区和被观测区之间的无缝空间一致性.

blocks.en: 2.3. Guidance for Denoising Optimization
blocks.zh: 2.3. 消除优化的指导

blocks.en: Extensive research ( Wang et al., 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2023b ; Ye et al., 2023 ; Lu et al., 2025b ; Zhong et al., 2025 ) has explored incorporating guidance during the denoising process to enhance fidelity relative to original inputs. Recent efforts ( Yang et al., 2025a ; Zhou and Tai, 2025 ; Li et al., 2026b ; Huang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ) have transitioned to the 3D domain. For instance, ReconViaGen ( Chang et al., 2025 ) Geometry Forcing ( Wu et al., 2025a ) and CUPID ( Huang et al., 2025a ) inject implicit features derived from pre-trained multi-view stereo models ( Wang et al., 2025 ) into generative pipelines to improve 3D consistency, but retain alignment errors due to spatial ambiguity and inaccurate predictions. In contrast, approaches like SAM3D ( Chen et al., 2025 ) and ShapeR ( Siddiqui et al., 2026 ) introduce explicit object point clouds as conditional inputs to constrain the spatial content. However, these feed-forward methods typically lack the per-scene precision required for complex environments. Unlike these approaches, our method employs an in-situ denoising optimization strategy driven by explicit spatial guidance. By treating explicit 3D guidance as persistent supervisory signals within an iterative loop, our framework progressively recovers missing textures and structures while adhering to the spatial evidence of the 3D scenes.

blocks.en: 3. Method
blocks.zh: 3个 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we first establish the basics of 3D representations and generative priors in Section 3.1 . Section 3.2 introduces a reformulated in-situ denoising optimization that bridges initial scene segments with 3D-native generative priors. To effectively regularize the optimization, Section 3.3 describes an adaptive guidance strategy using spatial anchors and temporal annealing. Section 3.4 details the overall pipeline of holistic object and background reconstruction.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们首先在第3.1节中确立了3D表达和基因前科的基本内容。 第3.2节引入了重新调整的场地解析优化,将初始场景部分与3D-原生地分层前身相接. 为了有效规范优化,第3.3节介绍了利用空间锚地和时间后退的适应性指导战略。 第3.4节详细介绍了整体目标和背景重建的总体管道。

blocks.en: 3.1. Preliminaries
blocks.zh: 3.1. 初步情况

blocks.en:
Our framework is built upon two design choices: a voxel-based scene representation and a 3D-native generative prior.
The use of a sparse voxel representation for decompositional reconstruction ensures a seamless connection with 3D generative priors, which operate on a structured voxel latent space. Furthermore, voxels provide a natural basis for incorporating our explicit 3D guidance introduced in Section 3.3 , allowing for precise and direct geometric anchoring throughout the optimization process.
Specifically, we adopt TRELLIS ( Xiang et al., 2025b ) as our generative prior, as its 3D-native architecture inherently ensures multi-view consistency. TRELLIS also provides joint modeling of both geometry and appearance, enabling our framework to simultaneously complete missing structures and synthesize consistent textures.

我们的框架建立在两个设计选择上:一个以活塞为主的场景代表,一个以3D为主的先生.
在分解重建中使用稀疏的活体代表,确保了与3D基因前科的无缝连接,这些前科在结构化活体潜伏空间上运行. 此外,花瓶为纳入我们在第3.3节中提出的明确的三维指导提供了自然基础,从而在整个优化过程中能够精确和直接地定位几何。
具体而言,我们采用TRELLIS(Xiang等人,2025年b)作为我们的先入之出,因为其3D-内在结构内在地确保多视角的一致性。 TRELLIS还提供几何和外观的联合模型,使我们能够的框架同时完成缺失的结构并合成一致的纹理.

Each voxel v i v_{i} is characterized by its center c i c_{i} , size s i s_{i} , density σ i \sigma_{i} , and spherical harmonic coefficients s ​ h i sh_{i} for appearance.
For each object k k , we identify its corresponding sparse voxel set 𝒱 k ⊂ 𝒱 \mathcal{V}_{k}\subset\mathcal{V} by fusing the 2D instance masks through volume fusion. Specifically, a voxel v i v_{i} is assigned to 𝒱 k \mathcal{V}_{k} if its projected 2D location consistently falls within the instance mask of object k k across multiple views.
Furthermore, we utilize the geometric uncertainty U g ​ e ​ o ​ m U_{geom} introduced in GeoSVR to quantify the confidence of the initial reconstruction, thereby identifying deterministic regions that serve as reliable spatial anchors.

blocks.en:
Our framework specifically utilizes three specialized modules from TRELLIS ( Xiang et al., 2025b ) : a sparse structure generation module G S G_{S} , a latent refinement module G L G_{L} , and a pre-trained VAE decoder 𝒟 v ​ a ​ e \mathcal{D}_{vae} .
The structure module G S G_{S} comprises an encoder ℰ \mathcal{E} , a decoder 𝒟 \mathcal{D} , and a structural flow model 𝐯 S \mathbf{v}_{S} . The encoder ℰ \mathcal{E} maps initial 3D representations ( e.g . , incomplete voxel sets 𝒱 k \mathcal{V}_{k} ) into the latent space. 𝐯 S \mathbf{v}_{S} iteratively refines the coarse geometric latents, and the decoder 𝒟 \mathcal{D} reconstructs the final geometry from the refined latents. The module G L G_{L} primarily governs the synthesis of object appearance by employing a latent flow model 𝐯 L \mathbf{v}_{L} to denoise the structured latents. Finally, the refined structured latents are passed through the VAE decoder 𝒟 v ​ a ​ e \mathcal{D}_{vae} to produce the final high-quality object mesh and its corresponding appearance.
For both G S G_{S} and G L G_{L} , the generation process is formulated as a conditional flow matching (CFM) problem ( Lipman et al., 2022 ) . Given a data distribution x 0 x_{0} and noise ϵ \epsilon , the model learns a vector field v θ ​ ( x t , t ) v_{\theta}(x_{t},t) to approximate the target velocity along the probability path x t = ( 1 − t ) ​ x 0 + t ​ ϵ x_{t}=(1-t)x_{0}+t\epsilon : (1) ℒ θ = 𝔼 t , x 0 , ϵ ​ ‖ v θ ​ ( x t , t ) − ( ϵ − x 0 ) ‖ 2 2 . \mathcal{L}_{\theta}=\mathbb{E}_{t,x_{0},\epsilon}\|v_{\theta}(x_{t},t)-(\epsilon-x_{0})\|_{2}^{2}.

blocks.zh: 3.2. 异地优化

blocks.en: A primary objective in decompositional reconstruction is to recover the complete geometry and appearance of individual objects from incomplete initial segments { 𝒱 k } \{\mathcal{V}_{k}\} . We formulate this completion as an in-situ denoising optimization within the scene-level coordinate space, leveraging a 3D-native generative prior.

blocks.en: 3.3. Adaptive Spatial Guidance
blocks.zh: 3.3. 适应性空间指导

blocks.en: To regularize the inherent stochasticity of 3D-native generative models, which often compromise the spatial fidelity of reconstructed objects, we propose an adaptive spatial guidance strategy to anchor the denoising process using spatial constraints and dynamically balance generative completion and structural preservation.
blocks.zh: 为了规范3D-内在基因模型的内在地貌特征,这往往会损害被重建的物体的空间忠诚性,我们提出了一个适应性的空间指导战略,利用空间约束和动态平衡基因完成和结构保存来固定去诺过程.

blocks.en: We enforce spatial fidelity by identifying two types of anchoring zones for each object: the occupied anchor ( Ω O \Omega_{O} ), representing regions where geometry is confidently reconstructed, and the vacant anchor ( Ω V \Omega_{V} ), representing regions where the object must not exist. Critically, the latent representation x ′ x^{\prime} in TRELLIS resides in a structured voxel feature space, where each voxel is associated with a 3D location through a deterministic mapping from real-world Euclidean coordinates to the latent feature. This spatial correspondence allows us to apply guidance directly to the latent features based on the underlying scene geometry.
blocks.zh: 我们通过确定每个对象的两类粘接区域来强制进行空间粘接: 占用的粘接区域 O\Omega\\O}, 代表有自信地对齐几何的区域, 和空的粘接区域 V\Omega\V} , 代表对象必须不存在的区域 。 关键的是,TRELLIS中的潜在代表x ' x^{\prime} 位于结构化的voxel地貌空间中,其中每个voxel通过从真实世界的欧克利得坐标到潜在地貌的确定性绘图与3D位置相联. 这种空间通信使我们能够直接将指导应用于基于地貌几何基础的潜在特征。

blocks.en:
While Ω O \Omega_{O} preserves existing structures, it cannot prevent the generative prior from hallucinating unwanted geometry in empty spaces. We therefore define the vacant anchor Ω V \Omega_{V} by fusing two sources of information: 1) free-space regions identified via ray-casting from input depth maps, and 2) regions occupied by the background or other objects.
A naive approach would be to prune the features in Ω V \Omega_{V} to zero. However, we observe that within the sparse latent space of the pre-trained prior, "inactive" regions—those representing empty space—do not possess zero-valued features. Instead, they follow a specific stochastic distribution characterized by a low-magnitude mean. Forcing these features to zero would push the latent state x ′ x^{\prime} off the learned manifold, leading to optimization instability and rendering artifacts.

虽然组合 O\Omega\\O} 保留了已有的结构, 但无法防止先基因在空格中逆行的几何 。 因此,我们通过使用两个信息来源来定义空置的粘合点 V\Omega_{V}: 1)通过输入深度图的射线广播确定的自由空间区域,2)被背景物体或其他物体所占据的区域.
一个天真的方法是将组合 V\Omega\V}中的特性推到零 。 然而,我们发现,在事先训练过的“不活跃”地区——代表空地的地区——的稀有潜在空间中,没有零价值的特征。 取而代之的是,它们遵循一个以低宽度平均值为特征的特定分层分布. 将这些特性加到零将使潜伏状态x ' x^{\prime' 脱离所学的多面体,导致最优化的不稳定性并制造出文物.

For each voxel 𝐯 ∈ Ω V \mathbf{v}\in\Omega_{V} , we compute a target mean μ n ​ e ​ w \mu_{new} by interpolating the current feature mean μ \mu toward a predefined near-zero prior mean μ 0 \mu_{0} : (5) μ n ​ e ​ w = ( 1 − λ p ) ​ μ + λ p ​ μ 0 , \mu_{new}=(1-\lambda_{p})\mu+\lambda_{p}\mu_{0}, where λ p ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] \lambda_{p}\in[0,1] is a redistribution factor. 4. Experiments

We evaluate DecomVoxel in terms of geometric reconstruction, appearance quality, and spatial fidelity. Additional details on the user-study protocol and significance tests, as well as limitations, are provided in supplementary .

4.1. Settings

We evaluate our method on 8 scenes from the synthetic Replica ( Straub et al., 2019 ) dataset and 6 real-world scenes from ScanNet++ ( Yeshwanth et al., 2023 ) , following ShapeR ( Siddiqui et al., 2026 ) . For each scene, we select every tenth view for testing and use the remaining views for training.

We adopt cd ( cd ), F-Score , and nc ( nc ) to evaluate reconstruction quality, and PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for rendering.
To further evaluate the perceptual quality of the reconstructed scenes, we conduct a user study to collect subjective scores from human subjects. Specifically, we focus on object geometry and appearance to evaluate the fidelity of individual entities, and spatial layout to assess whether the reconstructed results strictly adhere to the original scene.

We compare our framework against state-of-the-art decompositional reconstruction methods including SimRecon ( Xia et al., 2026 ) , ReconViaGen ( Chang et al., 2025 ) , CUPID ( Huang et al., 2025a ) , SAM3D ( Chen et al., 2025 ) , MV-SAM3D ( Li et al., 2026a ) , and ShapeR ( Siddiqui et al., 2026 ) . For methods requiring point cloud inputs, i.e . , SAM3D, MV-SAM3D, and ShapeR, we back-project depth estimated by Depth-Anything 3 ( Lin et al., 2025 ) using the corresponding camera poses and instance masks to ensure a high-quality geometric initialization for fair comparison. For ReconViaGen and CUPID, we follow their official multi-view inference procedures and align the outputs to scene coordinates with FoundationPose ( Wen et al., 2024 ) . Since ShapeR does not model appearance, we evaluate it only on geometry.
4.2. Results

As illustrated in Tables 1 , 4 , 7 and 6 , baselines that rely on decoupled 3D generation and post-hoc alignment, e.g . , SimRecon, ReconViaGen, and CUPID, do not optimize objects directly in the original scene coordinates. Without explicit scene-level constraints, they are more susceptible to geometric distortion and accumulated alignment errors. Meanwhile, methods that utilize 3D point clouds as feed-forward conditions, e.g . , SAM3D, MV-SAM3D, and ShapeR, frequently exhibit significant spatial drift in object position, rotation, and scale. These methods are also sensitive to input point-cloud density and may produce incomplete geometry on complex real-world datasets such as ScanNet++.
In contrast, our method achieves complete reconstruction while faithfully preserving the original spatial layout. By incorporating persistent explicit 3D guidance within the denoising optimization, we effectively anchor the stochasticity and inductive bias of the generative prior to the specific scene context.
This advantage is further supported by our user study in Table 2 , where human evaluators consistently favored our results for their high-quality reconstruction and precise spatial alignment.

Similar to our findings in geometry reconstruction, our guided denoising optimization significantly enhances appearance synthesis. Our method achieves style-consistent texture completion in unobserved regions while maintaining high consistency with original images in visible areas. Conversely, 3D-native baselines often produce textures that deviate obviously from the source style due to their lack of explicit appearance constraints, resulting in inferior rendering metrics. Qualitative assessments from human experts on texture consistency further validate that our optimization framework provides the most plausible appearance completion.

We conduct an in-depth analysis of our key design components, as visualized in Figure 5 . First, we investigate the impact of the distillation loss formulation. As illustrated by the convergence curves in Figure 5(a) , our proposed epsilon-based distillation loss facilitates a consistent and stable reduction in reconstruction error. In contrast, the naive velocity-based loss leads to significantly higher error in the later stages. This failure stems from an over-reliance on the flow matching model at high noise levels, where unstable optimization directions lead to sub-optimal local minima.
Furthermore, we validate the effectiveness of our temporal annealing strategies. As shown in Figure 5(b) , employing our linear noise sampling schedule results in a more stable and monotonic improvement in reconstruction quality compared to fixed noise levels. Regarding the spatial guidance in vacant regions, we observe that simply zeroing out latent features in these regions ( i.e . , Hard Prune) yields negligible improvements over no pruning in Figure 5(c) . Conversely, our re-distributed pruning strategy significantly enhances spatial fidelity by better aligning with the prior manifold. Finally, we examine the scheduling of the structural preservation loss weight w O w_{O} in Figure 5(d) . While this regularization consistently boosts performance, adopting an appropriate annealing schedule ( e.g . , Cosine or Cosine-power) further achieves a better trade-off between generative flexibility and structural persistence, leading to the highest reconstruction fidelity.
Additionally, Table 4 shows that our method trades longer runtime for better geometric completeness, texture consistency, and spatial alignment while maintaining comparable average memory.

4.3. Ablation Studies

Ablative studies, as shown in Table 3 , evaluate the contributions of the geometry prior ( GP ), appearance prior ( AP ), and their respective adaptive spatial guidance ( G-SG and A-SG ). Our analysis yields the following insights: • While incorporating the geometry prior ( GP ) improves reconstruction completeness, its inherent stochasticity often introduces geometric deviations from the original scene. Furthermore, using the appearance prior ( AP ) without guidance slightly degrades rendering performance, as unconstrained generation tends to conflict with the visual observation. • Integrating adaptive spatial guidance ( G-SG and A-SG ) consistently yields performance gains. These results demonstrate that by enforcing deterministic spatial anchors and dynamic scheduling for noise sampling, the guidance mechanism effectively suppresses the generative prior’s stochastic bias, ensuring both spatial and stylistic fidelity relative to the original scene. • Our full model achieves superior performance across all metrics, validating the synergistic effect of the entire guided denoising optimization. This demonstrates that our framework successfully balances generative capacity with strict adherence to scene constraints, achieving complete and faithful scene reconstruction.

5. Conclusion

In this work, we introduced DecomVoxel , a framework that establishes a principled bridge between 3D-native generative priors and neural scene reconstruction through guided in-situ denoising optimization. By integrating a reformulated epsilon-based distillation loss with adaptive spatial guidance, our approach suppresses generative hallucinations and mitigates spatial drift. Extensive evaluations on Replica and ScanNet++ demonstrate that DecomVoxel faithfully preserves structural fidelity and spatial layout, delivering textured meshes with clean topology, geometry, and appearance.
By providing a robust solution for recovering high-fidelity object entities within complex scenes, this framework has the potential to enhance the capacity to perceive and interact with the physical world in embodied AI and spatial intelligence.

B.1. Adaptive Spatial Guidance

Adaptive spatial guidance combines occupied and vacant anchors with temporal scheduling. Occupied anchors preserve reliable observations, while vacant anchors suppress occupancy in invalid regions. Their guidance is progressively relaxed alongside the denoising timestep, enabling a transition from observation preservation to prior-driven refinement.

Complementing Ω O \Omega_{O} , the vacant anchor Ω V \Omega_{V} identifies regions in which the target object should not generate geometry. We construct this vacant-space evidence from two sources. First, the GeoSVR depth maps and input cameras define a scene-level visibility grid at resolution R 3 R^{3} ( R = 256 R=256 in our experiments). Appendix C Evaluation Details
This section specifies the datasets, metrics, baseline settings, and user-study procedure used in the main evaluation.
C.1. Datasets

We evaluate on eight Replica ( Straub et al., 2019 ) scenes and six ScanNet++ ( Yeshwanth et al., 2023 ) scenes. Replica provides synthetic reference geometry and controlled renderings, while ScanNet++ contains real captures with incomplete and noisy observations. The same scene split, camera poses, and object masks are used for our method and all baselines. ScanNet++ uses the available dataset masks, which can be incomplete; the additional real-world qualitative examples use SAM2-generated masks ( Ravi et al., 2025 ) . These settings evaluate the method under moderate mask noise and occlusion without manually repairing every object mask.

C.4. Baseline Protocol

We use the official implementations and default model parameters for all baselines. For SimRecon ( Xia et al., 2026 ) and single-view SAM3D ( Chen et al., 2025 ) , we follow the unified view-selection protocol adopted by SimRecon. For SAM3D, MV-SAM3D ( Li et al., 2026a ) , and ShapeR ( Siddiqui et al., 2026 ) , we back-project depth maps estimated by Depth-Anything 3 ( Lin et al., 2025 ) within the same instance masks used by our method, transform the resulting points using the shared camera poses, and follow each method’s official input point-density setting.
For the object-centric generative baselines ReconViaGen ( Chang et al., 2025 ) and CUPID ( Huang et al., 2025a ) , which recover objects in method-specific coordinate systems, we follow their official multi-view inference procedures. Specifically, ReconViaGen recovers geometry in the VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) coordinate system, whereas CUPID reconstructs each object relative to its input camera coordinates. We then align their outputs with the scene coordinate system using FoundationPose ( Wen et al., 2024 ) .
C.5. User Study Protocol

The user study contains 44 questionnaires completed by 44 unique expert raters. Each questionnaire contains 25 questions: 10 on object geometry, 10 on object appearance, and 5 on scene layout. Object questions are sampled uniformly from the objects in the eight Replica and six ScanNet++ scenes. Layout questions are sampled uniformly from the same 14 scenes.

The study is blind and randomized: method identities are hidden and presentation order is randomized. Object-geometry questions ask raters to assess geometric completeness and consistency with the visible evidence; object-appearance questions assess texture quality and consistency with observed views; scene-layout questions assess agreement of position, rotation, and scale with the input scene. Scores use a five-point scale, as reported in the main paper.

In addition to mean scores, we test whether our method is preferred to a competing baseline more often than chance. We use two-sided exact binomial tests with null probability p = 0.5 p=0.5 . The preferences are significant for scene layout, object geometry, and object appearance, with p p -values 8.45 × 10 − 75 8.45\times 10^{-75} , 1.50 × 10 − 58 1.50\times 10^{-58} , and 4.26 × 10 − 36 4.26\times 10^{-36} , respectively. Appendix D Limitations and Future Work

Our method relies on an initial GeoSVR reconstruction, object masks, and a pretrained 3D prior. Although our experiments on the real-world ScanNet++ scenes demonstrate robustness to incomplete masks and occlusion, severely inaccurate masks, poor initialization, or extreme occlusion may still leave insufficient reliable evidence for occupied anchors, while objects outside the prior distribution may not be faithfully completed.

Moreover, the current implementation uses the object-centric TRELLIS prior and has been evaluated primarily on indoor scenes with well-defined object instances. The in-situ formulation is not tied to a particular generative model and could therefore incorporate stronger and more diverse 3D priors. This offers a promising path toward larger or outdoor environments, such as street scenes, provided that reliable initial reconstruction and object decomposition are available. Regions that cannot be meaningfully decomposed into objects, such as sky or grassland, remain outside the current scope and may instead benefit from scene-level generative priors ( Wu et al., 2024 ) .

A further practical limitation is computational cost. Per-object geometry and appearance optimization is slower than a single feed-forward pass, although multiple objects can be optimized in parallel. Future work could reduce latency by distilling the optimization process or developing more efficient guidance schedules while preserving reconstruction quality and spatial fidelity.
